intro: Lisbon rewards visitors with tiled alleys, river views and custard tarts at every turn. Pick how long you have and what you enjoy most.
tour_note: Check the tour page for which entry tickets are included.

notes: Metro is fast and cheap; red line links the airport to the centre with one change.
Carris buses and trams cover the city; buy a rechargeable Navegante card for about €0.50.
Trams 15 and 28 are scenic but crowded; watch for pickpockets.
Taxis use meters; insist on the meter and keep a receipt.
Uber, Bolt and FreeNow work in Lisbon; look for the TVDE sign on the car.
Driving in the centre is slow and parking is hard; walking and bikes work well on flat Baixa.

belem_tower.name: Belém Tower
belem_tower.hours: Tue–Sun roughly 10:00–17:30 · closed Mondays · check on the day
belem_tower.tip: Go right at opening or late afternoon; the spiral stairs are narrow and queues grow fast.

jeronimos.name: Jerónimos Monastery
jeronimos.price_text: ≈ €12 adult · cloister included · check on the day
jeronimos.tip: Buy a timed ticket online the day before; the cloister is the highlight, not the church.

sao_jorge.name: São Jorge Castle
sao_jorge.hours: Daily roughly 09:00–21:00 in summer · shorter in winter
sao_jorge.tip: Come for the terrace views over Alfama and the river, not the small museum.

praca_comercio.name: Praça do Comércio
praca_comercio.price_text: Free to walk · arch viewpoint charged separately
praca_comercio.tip: Sit by the river steps at sunset; the square is the natural start of a Baixa walk.

padrao.name: Padrão dos Descobrimentos
padrao.price_text: ≈ €6 adult · rooftop included · check on the day
padrao.tip: The rooftop gives the best view back to Belém Tower and the river.

santa_justa.name: Santa Justa Lift
santa_justa.tip: Skip the lift queue and walk up through Chiado to the top terrace instead.

alfama.name: Alfama District
alfama.tip: Get lost on purpose; the steep lanes and tiled walls are the point. Wear grippy shoes.

bacalhau.name: Bacalhau à Brás
bacalhau.hours: Lunch and dinner · varies by restaurant
bacalhau.tip: Order it in a simple neighbourhood tasca, not a tourist-menu place on the main square.

bairro_alto.name: Bairro Alto
bairro_alto.hours: Quiet by day · bars busiest roughly 22:00–02:00
bairro_alto.tip: Come after 22:00 for street bars; keep noise down, locals live here.

pasteis_belem.name: Pastéis de Belém
pasteis_belem.tip: Take the takeaway counter at the side; the sit-down queue is much slower.

cascais.name: Cascais Beach
cascais.hours: Beach always open · lifeguards in summer
cascais.tip: Take the train from Cais do Sodré; the coast here is calmer than Atlantic beaches further west.

moors_castle.name: Castle of the Moors
moors_castle.tip: A Sintra day trip: walk the forest path up from the old town, it is steep but shady.

chiado.name: Chiado District
chiado.tip: Coffee at a historic café, then browse the bookshops and side streets.

alvalade.name: Estádio José Alvalade
alvalade.price_text: Stadium tour price varies · check on the day
alvalade.hours: Tour times vary on match weeks
alvalade.tip: Book a stadium tour online; match tickets sell out and prices change.

luz.name: Estádio da Luz
luz.price_text: Tour price varies · check on the day
luz.hours: Tour times vary on match weeks
luz.tip: Check the fixture list first; tours pause around home games.

ler_devagar.name: Ler Devagar
ler_devagar.hours: Roughly Tue–Sun 10:00–20:00 · check on the day
ler_devagar.tip: A bookshop inside an old factory in LX Factory; go for the space and the café.

zoo.name: Lisbon Zoo
zoo.price_text: ≈ €26 adult · child rates lower · check on the day
zoo.tip: Good for families; allow half a day and bring water in summer.

mafra.name: Mafra Palace Library
mafra.price_text: ≈ €6 palace ticket · check on the day
mafra.tip: A half-day trip outside Lisbon; the long rococo library is the reason to come.

azulejo.name: National Azulejo Museum
azulejo.tip: The huge tile panel of old Lisbon is the highlight; quiet and uncrowded.

coach_museum.name: National Coach Museum
coach_museum.tip: Pair with Belém sights; the gilded royal coaches surprise most visitors.

oceanario.name: Oceanário de Lisboa
oceanario.price_text: ≈ €25 adult · child rates lower · check on the day
oceanario.tip: Buy a timed ticket online; the big central tank is worth a slow sit-down.

pena.name: Pena Palace
pena.price_text: ≈ €20 palace and park · check on the day
pena.tip: Book a timed ticket; mornings are clearer and less crowded than midday.

time_out_market.name: Time Out Market
time_out_market.tip: One roof, many top chefs; go off-peak to find seats.

senhora_monte.name: Senhora do Monte viewpoint
senhora_monte.tip: The highest miradouro in the city; come at sunset with a drink from a nearby kiosk.

tram28.name: Tram 28 ride
tram28.price_text: ≈ €3 single on board · day pass cheaper
tram28.tip: Board at the Martim Moniz end early to get a seat; watch for pickpockets.

fado_show.name: Fado show in Alfama
fado_show.price_text: ≈ €20–40 with a drink · dinner packages cost more
fado_show.tip: Small rooms sound better than big venues; book ahead in summer.

lx_factory.name: LX Factory walk
lx_factory.price_text: Free to walk · food and shops extra
lx_factory.tip: Old industrial yard with shops and food; combine with a riverside walk.

miradouro_santa_luzia.name: Miradouro de Santa Luzia
miradouro_santa_luzia.tip: Tiled terrace with river views; a calm stop while walking Alfama.

stays.why: Flat, central grid near the river, tram 15 and metro. Easiest base for first-timers and walking.
Oldest quarter, steep lanes and fado bars. Charming but hilly and noisy at night.
Upscale shopping and cafés, walkable to Baixa and Bairro Alto. Good mix of comfort and location.
Nightlife heart; quiet by day, loud on weekend nights. Close to Chiado and Príncipe Real.

food: Try a pastel de nata warm with cinnamon; the famous Belém bakery queues are long, many cafés are just as good.
Eat grilled sardines and bacalhau (salt cod) in a simple tasca; lunch menus often cost €8–15.
Order a bifana (pork sandwich) or a prego for a cheap snack, about €3–6.
Seafood is best near the river and in Cascais; check the price per kilo before ordering.
Vegetarian and vegan options are growing in Chiado and Príncipe Real; check menus on the day.
more_time: Swap a city day for Sintra: train from Rossio, about 40 minutes, to palaces and gardens. Go early, it gets crowded.
Take a half-day trip to Cascais or Belém by train along the river for beaches and the tower.
Spend an evening in a fado house in Alfama or Mouraria; book ahead and expect a cover charge.
